pages.text: Mars is much smaller than Earth, so why is the amount of land surface of these planets nearly the same? Take a look at the picture of Earth below. See all that blue? Most of the Earth’s surface is covered by water. Mars is a desert planet. Its surface is not covered by water. This helped explain why the surface of Mars is so dry. Water freezes or evaporates in the dry, cold air of Mars. The dry soil and lack of water cause heavy dust storms on large areas of the planet. Martian Moons The two Martian moons are called Phobos (FOH-bohs) and Deimos (DEE-mohs). These are Greek words meaning “fear” and “panic.” Phobos and Deimos were the twin sons of the Greek god of war, Ares.
pages.brief: Earth appears blue with most of its surface covered by water, while smaller Mars looks dry and desert-like. Dust storms sweep across Mars. Two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, hover nearby; in Greek myth they were twin sons of the war god Ares.

pages.text: The 1976 Viking mission was made up of two spacecraft. It was the first mission to land on the surface of Mars. Both spacecraft looked for signs of life by testing soil samples. In 1976, the Viking 2 rover landed on Mars and took samples of the surface. It sent information back to scientists on Earth. The scientists learned that the rusty red color was due to large amounts of iron, a metal, in the soil. Viking also reported no signs of organic matter—the remains of living things. Mars seemed to be a dry, desert planet.
pages.brief: In 1976, two Viking spacecraft arrive at Mars, and Viking 2 lands on the surface to take soil samples. The rusty red soil is found to contain iron, a metal. Tests report no signs of organic matter, making Mars seem like a dry, desert planet.

pages.text: Would I be weightless on Mars? No, but you would weigh less because you would experience less than half the gravity you do on Earth. Scientists were still puzzled, though. Canyons on Earth are formed by running water. Mars looked like Earth without water. In 1997, the Mars Pathfinder also found rocks that seemed to have been shaped by water. Could Mars have had water long ago?
pages.brief: A person stands on Mars and feels lighter, because gravity there is less than half of Earth’s. Nearby, rocks found by the 1997 Mars Pathfinder appear shaped by water. Since canyons on Earth are formed by running water, scientists wonder if Mars once had water.

pages.text: Curiosity, a car-sized rover, launched in 2011. Its mission was to see if Mars could have supported small life- forms called microbes, and if humans could survive there someday! Looking for Answers In 2003, the European Space Agency (ESA) launched the Mars Express. This spacecraft would orbit Mars and collect information about the planet. Just one month after arriving at Mars, Mars Express found ice at the planet’s south pole. This meant there was water on Mars.
pages.brief: A car-sized rover named Curiosity travels toward Mars after launching in 2011, seeking signs that microbes could have lived there and whether humans could survive. The Mars Express spacecraft orbits the planet and finds ice at the south pole, meaning there is water on Mars.

pages.text: How long is a day on Mars? A Martian day is just a bit longer than an Earth day—24 hours and 37 minutes. For the next several years, the Mars Express studied the planet’s south pole. In July 2018, European scientists said they had found a saltwater lake underneath about 2 kilometers (1 mi.) of ice on the surface of Mars. They think this lake is 20 kilometers (12 mi.) wide. Scientists think there may be other lakes, too, that might even contain life. In 2012 NASA sent the Curiosity rover to Mars. Curiosity tested samples of the soil and air on Mars. The air samples contained a gas called methane. On Earth, tiny living things called microbes make methane. Scientists wondered if the same might be true on Mars.
pages.brief: A Martian day passes over the planet, lasting 24 hours and 37 minutes, while the Mars Express studies the south pole. Beneath about two kilometers of ice, scientists find a saltwater lake twenty kilometers wide. The Curiosity rover tests soil and air, finding methane gas.

pages.text: Scientists can’t say for sure if life really did or does exist on Mars. More Mars missions are planned for 2020 and beyond. These missions will send rovers to look for signs of life. They will also gather information to see if it might be possible for people to someday live there. Perhaps one day, Mars will be inhabited by intelligent beings—from Earth!
pages.brief: Scientists look toward future Mars missions planned for 2020 and beyond, when rovers will search for signs of life and gather information about whether people could live there. Mars waits in space, perhaps one day to be inhabited by intelligent beings—from Earth.
